verdict.rationale: Homebrew documents project dependencies in a Brewfile, installed with one command, usable in scripts and CI such as GitHub Actions. The `brew bundle check || brew bundle install` pattern shows exit status can drive scripted control flow, and NONINTERACTIVE=1 and `--yes` support unattended runs. Missing for 10: explicit documentation of exit-code semantics and failure/error output for install and upgrade, documented non-interactive updating of Brewfile dependencies, and independent hands-on corroboration of agent/CI reliability.

support.subject: As an AI-native user, I can have an agent install and update project dependencies non-interactively, with clear exit codes and errors when something fails

citations.quote: You can use this behaviour in scripts like so: brew bundle check || brew bundle install
one command can set up project dependencies across these environments and in continuous-integration services such as GitHub Actions.
Use this from administrative scripts when the desktop user manages Homebrew, for example `brew as-console-user install --yes` formula.
this will take instructions from the Brewfile to run brew install ruby and install Ruby if needed
